explanations.answer: Send him back the way he came
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. The LORD says, “I will send you back the way you came.” Sennacherib, Assyria's king, showed up thinking he'd walk into Jerusalem. With a hook in his nose and a bit in his mouth, he's the one being steered.

explanations.answer: Lead him into Jerusalem in chains
explanations.explanation: That's not what the LORD says, friend. He says, “I will send you back the way you came.” Later in this same message, the LORD says Sennacherib, Assyria's king, “will not enter this city” (Isaiah 37:34). So there's no walking into Jerusalem at all.

explanations.answer: Hand him over to the king of Egypt
explanations.explanation: Egypt's king isn't in this verse, baker. The LORD says, “I will send you back the way you came.” Sennacherib, Assyria's king, is headed back the way he arrived, not handed to anybody.

explanations.answer: They will sow and reap again
explanations.explanation: That's the turn, baker. The sign says, “But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.” Two years of eating what grows on its own, then back to planting and harvesting. Hezekiah, Judah's king, gets a clear schedule for a recovery.

explanations.answer: They will leave the land for good
